column1: # The porting verdicts of the NPC kernel's closure, one row per retail function.
# ledger joined with this overlay, and `coverage.md`'s `## Verdicts by layer band` counts it. The
# verdict lives here rather than in the rendered table because the table is rewritten from the
# corpus on every run and a verdict is a reading that must survive that.
#   address   the retail function, lower-case, no `0x`
#   verdict   rule | mechanism | present | dead | unsettled
#   band      the `order.md` layer band the row was verdicted in (`0-4`, `5-9`, …)
#   target    rule: the port method that carries the body. mechanism: the Unreal service or port
#             seam. present: the port function that already runs it. dead: `-`.
#   evidence  one line: the reason, or the automation test a `rule` row's port is covered by

Slot 589, 830 bytes only because the stat-list lookup is inlined six times. Each lookup scans the NPC's stat-list array (count at +0x13bc, pointer table at +0x13c0) for the first entry whose type word at +0x10 equals 3 (the scripted list) or 2 (the buff list), and falls back to the lazily constructed global CVStatList_t at DAT_109f0b40 (guard bit 0 of DAT_109f0b2a, registered with atexit 0x10012a8a) when none matches. Body: base = CVStatList_t::GetBase(list3, statId); when the new value is greater than base, look up the type-2 list and, only when its GetBase(statId) is below the new value, CVStatList_t::Set(list2, statId, value), then CVStatList_t::AddBase(list3, statId, value - base) and then CVStatList_t::Set(list3, statId, value); when the new value is less than base, CVStatList_t::Set(list3, statId, value) first and then CVStatList_t::SubBase(list3, statId, base - value); equal values write nothing at all.
